scope.q: What is the typical complexity and variability of these reporting rules, e.g., are they quantitative thresholds, specific qualitative narratives, or a mix, and how frequently do they change?
scope.why: Understanding the nature and dynamism of the rules is critical to determining the complexity of rule extraction, validation, and the system's adaptability.

scope.q: What are the downstream consequences of a missed or incorrect report, and how critical is auditability and traceability for each data point back to its source?
scope.why: This defines the acceptable error tolerance, the required rigor for data provenance, and the necessary validation steps, which impacts architecture and testing efforts.

scope.q: Who are the primary users of the current reporting system (the one person, grant managers, auditors, executives) and what specific actions do they need to perform beyond just report generation?
scope.why: Identifying all stakeholders and their workflows helps define the necessary UI, access controls, and integration points, ensuring the solution addresses actual user needs.

decomposition.title: Rule Extraction & Normalization
decomposition.why: This subproblem focuses on converting unstructured spreadsheet data into a structured, machine-readable format for rule definition.

decomposition.title: Reporting Rule Engine
decomposition.why: This piece will implement the core logic to evaluate grant data against the normalized reporting rules and determine compliance.

decomposition.title: Data Ingestion & Harmonization
decomposition.why: This involves collecting relevant grant and financial data from various sources and preparing it for evaluation by the rule engine.

decomposition.title: Reporting & Visualization UI
decomposition.why: This covers the user interface for viewing report statuses, generating reports, and interacting with the system's outputs.

decomposition.title: Audit & Compliance Logging
decomposition.why: This component is essential for tracking all rule evaluations, data changes, and report generations to ensure full auditability.

sprint.title: Initial Rule Schema & Data Ingest POC
sprint.deliv: Defined JSON schema for a sample reporting rule and a script to ingest a small dataset from a CSV into a local database.

sprint.title: Core Rule Engine Logic
sprint.deliv: Working Python function that takes structured rule and data, and returns a boolean compliance check for a single rule.

sprint.title: Basic Reporting Service & API
sprint.deliv: A REST API endpoint that accepts grant ID, runs the rule engine, and returns compliance status for specified rules.

sprint.title: Simple UI for Report View
sprint.deliv: A basic web page that can display the compliance status for a grant by calling the reporting service API.

sprint.title: Audit Logging Integration
sprint.deliv: Rule engine and reporting service write evaluation and generation events to a persistent log, accessible via a simple query.

sprint.title: Rule Editor Prototype
sprint.deliv: A UI form that allows creation/editing of one type of structured reporting rule, stored in the rule store.

sprint.title: End-to-End Demo Preparation
sprint.deliv: A functional demo showing rule definition, data ingestion, compliance check, and report display for 2-3 sample grants.

risks.risk: The existing 'one person's' knowledge is highly tacit and difficult to codify into explicit rules, leading to incomplete or incorrect rule definitions.
risks.mitigation: Conduct extensive, structured interviews with the subject matter expert, using concrete examples to extract rule logic. Implement a robust rule testing framework with historical data for validation.

risks.risk: Grant reporting rules are more complex and nuanced than anticipated (e.g., temporal dependencies, conditional logic, fuzzy matching), making the rule engine design too simplistic.
risks.mitigation: Start with a flexible, extensible rule engine architecture (e.g., a rules engine library or a DSL) that can accommodate increasing complexity. Prioritize rule discovery to identify edge cases early.

risks.risk: Integrating with various, potentially messy, internal data sources (ERP, financial systems) proves challenging, leading to data quality issues and delays.
risks.mitigation: Perform a thorough data source audit early to understand formats, APIs, and data quality. Prioritize building robust ETL pipelines with data validation and error handling from day one.

risks.risk: Adoption by grant managers is low due to a clunky UI or a lack of trust in the system's accuracy compared to their current manual processes.
risks.mitigation: Involve grant managers in UI/UX design from early stages. Implement parallel reporting for a period, comparing system outputs with manual reports to build confidence and refine accuracy.
